name: Corn Plant
description: Dracaena fragrans (corn plant) is a popular tropical houseplant in the Asparagaceae family, native to Africa and islands in the Indian Ocean. It has a sturdy cane-like stem and arching, glossy green leaves that can be solid or variegated depending on cultivar. It tolerates low to bright indirect light and average indoor humidity, making it a durable choice for homes and offices. It prefers well-draining, peat-based soil and moderate watering—allow the top of the soil to dry between waterings. All parts are toxic to cats and dogs if ingested; keep away from pets.
careTips: Bright indirect light is ideal; tolerates low light and fluorescent office light
Water when the top 1–2 inches of soil are dry; avoid soggy or waterlogged soil
Use well-draining potting mix with peat and perlite
Average room humidity (40–50%) is fine; avoid very dry or drafty spots
Keep temperatures between 15–24 °C; avoid cold drafts
Fertilize lightly with balanced liquid fertilizer every few weeks in growing season
Toxic to cats and dogs—keep out of reach of pets
